notes: All numbers are tagged with a 'confidence' of 'sourced' (taken from a fetched source page), 'derived' (computed from a sourced formula) or 'unverified' / 'somaxHeuristic' (our own engineering choice or a figure we could not confirm on a fetched page).
Distances in metres/km, times in seconds, paces in seconds per km unless stated.

benchmarks.label: 5 km time
benchmarks.howToTest: All-out solo time trial or parkrun/5K race on a flat course after 10-15 min easy warm-up incl. 3-4 strides. Use a race or time trial from the last 6 weeks. GPS distance must be 4.95-5.10 km; otherwise prorate.

benchmarks.label: 1 mile / 1600 m time
benchmarks.howToTest: Track time trial, 4 laps + 9 m (or 4 laps for 1600 m) after warm-up. Converted to 5K-equivalent via VDOT.

benchmarks.label: 10 km time
benchmarks.howToTest: Race or solo time trial. Converted to VDOT.

benchmarks.label: Half marathon time
benchmarks.howToTest: Race result from the last 12 weeks.

benchmarks.label: Marathon time
benchmarks.howToTest: Race result from the last 16 weeks.

benchmarks.label: Longest continuous easy run
benchmarks.howToTest: How long can you jog without walking at a conversational pace? Used to place new runners (under 30 min continuous = Couch-to-5K style walk/run start).

benchmarks.label: Average weekly running distance (last 4 weeks)
benchmarks.howToTest: Average of the last 4 weeks from the watch/app log. Caps the starting volume.

benchmarks.label: Longest single run in last 4 weeks
benchmarks.howToTest: From log. Caps the first long run.

levelPlacement.description: Level = the LOWER of (performance level from 5K-equivalent time) and (history level from volume/consistency). A runner who cannot run 30 min continuously is 'new' regardless of anything else.
levelPlacement.conversion: Any race benchmark is converted to VDOT with paceModel.formulas, then to a 5K-equivalent time.

newRunner.rule: continuous-run-minutes < 30 OR cannot complete 5 km without walking
newRunner.plan: Couch-to-5K walk/run progression (sessionTemplates c25k-*) before any pace-based training

performanceBySex.basis: Percentiles of 2018 US 5K race finishers (RunRepeat, ~2.6M participants; parkrun excluded). Median men 31:18, women 36:24; 10th-fastest-percentile men 22:06, women 25:16; 30th men 26:48, women 30:41.
performanceBySex.confidence: sourced (percentiles); the cut points chosen are a somaxHeuristic

historyLevel.intermediate: >= 12 months running 3-4 days/week AND 20-40 km/week (Higdon's Intermediate 5K prerequisite is 1-2 years at 3-4 days/week, 15-20 miles/week)
historyLevel.advanced: >= 24 months AND > 40 km/week (Pfitzinger's lowest 10K schedule expects 25-35 miles/week already)
historyLevel.confidence: thresholds partly sourced (Higdon, Pfitzinger prerequisites), cut points somaxHeuristic

ageAndSex.method: WMA age-grading: age-grade % = age-and-sex standard time / runner's time. Class bands (USATF Masters): 60%+ local, 70%+ regional, 80%+ national, 90%+ world class.
ageAndSex.suggestedUse: For runners 40+, if age grade >= 60% place at least 'intermediate'; >= 70% 'advanced'. Factor tables (WMA 2023) not bundled here.
ageAndSex.confidence: class bands sourced; mapping to levels somaxHeuristic; factor tables not fetched (unverified)

paceModel.method: Daniels/Gilbert VDOT. Compute VDOT from any recent race, then derive training paces as speeds that correspond to a fraction of VDOT on the oxygen-cost curve.

formulas.oxygenCost: VO2(v) = -4.60 + 0.182258*v + 0.000104*v^2   (v in metres/min, VO2 in ml/kg/min)
formulas.equivalentRaceTime: Solve VDOT(distance, t) = runnerVDOT for t (bisection, 1..900 min).
formulas.checks: 10K in 40:00 -> VO2 47.46, F 0.914, VDOT ~51.9 (matches billmill worked example). 5K 20:00 -> VDOT 49.8.
formulas.confidence: sourced formula (billmill notes + multiple calculator pages, originating in Daniels & Gilbert 1979 'Oxygen Power')

easy.use: easy, recovery, warm-up, cool-down, long runs
easy.sourceRange: Daniels: E = 59-74% VO2max; 0.63-0.73 calibrated so VDOT 51 gives 4:52-5:29/km as in Daniels' Table 5.2 excerpt

long.note: long runs are E pace; first half at the slow end

marathon.rule: equivalent marathon race pace at current VDOT
marathon.sourceRange: Daniels M = 75-84% VO2max; VDOT 51 -> 4:27/km matches book excerpt

threshold.sourceRange: Daniels T 'comfortably hard', ~1 hour race effort; 0.88 reproduces VDOT 51 -> 4:11/km from book excerpt

interval.sourceRange: Daniels I = 95-100% VO2max; 0.975 reproduces VDOT 51 -> 3:51/km from book excerpt. One third-party calculator gives ~5 s/km faster at VDOT 40 (unverified).

rep.rule: faster of (equivalent 1-mile race pace) and (interval pace x 0.95, i.e. >=5% faster than I) at current VDOT
rep.sourceRange: Daniels R = 105-120% VO2max, short reps (200-600 m) with full recovery. Mile-race-pace approximation is unverified against Daniels' printed R column.

race.rule: goal race pace (target time / distance) — only used in peak-phase race-pace sessions

rules: Train at CURRENT fitness (latest test VDOT), not goal VDOT; goal pace appears only in race-pace reps (unverified attribution to Daniels, standard coaching practice).
Without a new test, raise VDOT by at most 1 point every 4-6 weeks and only if sessions are going well (Daniels, Ask Dr Jack Daniels Q&A — sourced).
With a new race/time trial, reset VDOT to the result (up or down).
Riegel T2 = T1*(D2/D1)^1.06 may be shown as a cross-check for equivalent times (valid ~3.5-230 min); it predicts optimistically for long distances, so VDOT equivalence is the default.
New runners (slower than ~35:00 5K or 'new' level): pace targets are advisory only; prescribe by effort (talk test) and walk/run.
Adjust paces slower in heat/altitude (McMillan calculator supports this; no specific coefficients sourced).
paceModel.tableNote: Rows with extrapolated=true (VDOT < 30) lie below the range covered by most published VDOT tables; values are formula extrapolations — treat as effort guides.

evidence.fact: Daniels: without a race, raise VDOT by ~1 point every 4-6 weeks at most (~0.17-0.25 VDOT/week).
Gunnarsson & Bangsbo 2012: 7 weeks of 10-20-30 training in moderately trained runners improved 5 km by 48 s (VO2max +4%).
Gliemann et al.: 160 recreational runners, 8 weeks 10-20-30, 5 km improved 38 s.
Beginners improve faster than trained runners in absolute terms; no fetched source gave a % figure for novices.

vdotGainPerWeek.confidence: somaxHeuristic, calibrated so intermediate rates sit inside Daniels' 1 VDOT / 4-6 wk and the 10-20-30 trial results; beginner rate is higher (unverified)
vdotGainPerWeek.integration: Simulate week by week: vdot += gain(vdot) * daysMultiplier; rate is re-looked-up each week so improvement slows as the runner gets fitter.

algorithm: 1. currentVdot = VDOT(benchmark); targetVdot = VDOT(goal distance, goal time).
2. If targetVdot <= currentVdot: goal already met at current fitness -> offer a maintenance/sharpening plan of minWeeks, or suggest a harder goal.
3. buildWeeks = number of simulated weeks until vdot >= targetVdot (expected scenario).
4. totalWeeks = buildWeeks + taperWeeks(goal distance), then clamp to [minWeeks(goal), maxBlockWeeks(level)].

5. If buildWeeks + taper > maxBlockWeeks: STEPPING-STONE. Block 1 goal = time equivalent to the VDOT reachable in maxBlockWeeks (conservative scenario, rounded to a friendly time e.g. nearest :30). After block 1, retest and generate the next block.
6. If total weeks across all blocks > 52, mark goal 'long-term'; show the first stepping stone only and say the final goal is a 1-year+ target.
7. Re-plan after every retest (every 4-6 weeks): recompute paces and remaining weeks; shorten or extend within clamps.

workedExamples.result: 24 simulated build weeks (+1 taper) > 16-week block -> STEPPING STONE. Block 1 = 16 weeks; conservative scenario reaches VDOT ~35.2 (~26:50), so block-1 goal = 27:00. Retest, then Block 2 (~8-10 weeks) to 25:00. Starts with easy volume + strides; threshold from build phase.
28 build weeks; Block 1 conservative ~27:15 -> goal 27:30, then Block 2.
7 build weeks + 1 taper = 8 weeks. Short base (2 wk), then threshold, VO2max intervals and goal-pace reps.
27 build weeks -> 2 blocks: Block 1 (16 wk) to ~21:00-21:15, Block 2 to sub-20.
~56 weeks -> 'long-term' goal (>52 wk). Show first stepping stone (~19:30) only.

5kFinishBeginner.prereq: some jogging experience; can run ~1.5 miles (2.4 km)

marathonFinish.prereq: first-time marathoners; regular running base (half marathon experience recommended — somaxHeuristic)

startingWeeklyKm.rule: start = min(table value, 1.1 * reported weekly-distance-km); if no history, use the low end
startingWeeklyKm.anchors: Higdon Novice 5K week 1 = 4.5 miles (7.2 km) over 3 runs (sourced); Higdon Intermediate 5K prereq 15-20 mi/wk (24-32 km, sourced); Pfitzinger 10K schedules start at 30/45/60 mi/wk (48/72/97 km, sourced). Ranges between anchors are somaxHeuristic.

peakWeeklyKm.anchors: Higdon Novice 5K peak ~8 mi run (+walk); Novice HM peak ~20-23 mi (32-37 km); Novice 1 Marathon peak ~40 mi (64 km); Pfitzinger 10K peaks 42/57/76 mi (67/92/122 km). Other ranges somaxHeuristic.
peakWeeklyKm.rule: also cap peak at the volume the days available can hold: maxKm = days * 90 min * (easy pace)

progression.weeklyIncrease: +5-10% per week (default 8%); for weekly volume < 20 km allow +2 km absolute instead
hardCaps: never > +10% week-on-week for 'new'/'beginner' after the walk/run phase
never > +30% over any 2-week window (Nielsen 2014: >30% over 2 weeks associated with more injuries vs <10%)
progression.evidenceNote: Buist 2008 RCT (532 novices): a graded 10%-rule programme (13 wk) had the same injury rate (20.8%) as a standard 8-week programme (20.3%, ~24% weekly increases). The 10% rule is a conservative default, not a proven threshold.

longRun.shareOfWeek: <= 25-30% of weekly km when weekly km <= ~64 (Daniels)
longRun.increase: +1-2 km per week (Higdon novice plans add ~0.25-0.5 mi/week on 5K, ~1 mi/week on half/marathon)

intensityCaps.interval: <= 8% of weekly km and <= 10 km per session
intensityCaps.rep: <= 5% of weekly km and <= 8 km per session
intensityCaps.easyShare: >= 80% of weekly time at easy/low intensity (Seiler; Fitzgerald 80/20)

cutbackWeeks.rule: every 3rd week for new/beginner and marathon plans (Higdon Novice 1 Marathon uses every 3rd week); every 4th week otherwise
cutbackWeeks.reduction: reduce volume 20-30%, keep one light quality session
cutbackWeeks.confidence: pattern sourced (Higdon); size of reduction unverified

taper.evidence: Bosquet 2007 meta-analysis: ~2-week taper, volume reduced 41-60% (progressive/exponential), intensity and frequency maintained.

rules.5k: last 7-10 days: volume -30-50%, keep 1 short sharp session (e.g. 4-6 x 400 at race pace)
rules.marathon: 3 weeks (Higdon): week -3 ~80%, -2 ~60%, race week ~40% of peak (percentages somaxHeuristic, within Bosquet range)

taper.keep: same number of run days; keep some race-pace work; drop long run length first

safety.rule: Health screen: no major health problems / clearance if unsure before starting (Higdon prerequisite).

New runners start with walk/run (C25K: 1 min run / 1.5 min walk, 3x/week, rest day between) and only progress when the current week feels manageable; repeating a week is allowed (NHS says you can take longer than 9 weeks).
Weekly volume: default +<=10%/week; never > +30% over any 2 weeks (Nielsen 2014). The 10% rule itself has weak evidence (Buist 2008) so it is a conservative default.
Novices have ~2.3x the injury rate of recreational runners per 1000 h (17.8 vs 7.7; Videbaek 2015) — beginners get extra rest days and no back-to-back hard days.
>= 80% of training time at easy intensity; easy = conversational (Seiler, Fitzgerald 80/20, Higdon).
Quality volume caps per session: T <= 10%, I <= 8% (and <= 10 km), R <= 5% (and <= 8 km) of weekly km (Daniels).
Long run <= 25-30% of weekly km (when <= ~64 km/week) and <= 150 min (Daniels E caps).
Pace increases: no more than +1 VDOT per 4-6 weeks without a test (Daniels).
No structured intervals for 'new' runners until they can run 30 min continuously; first quality is strides/fartlek.
Pain that changes your gait, or that worsens during a run, = stop and rest; persistent pain > 3 days = see a professional.
Missed >= 2 weeks: resume at ~50-70% of previous volume and retest before using old paces.
Hot/humid or altitude: run by effort, slow paces.
safety.confidence: McMillan supports heat/altitude adjustment; no coefficients sourced
